newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan firm sets leasing deal with McDonnell.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan firm sets leasing deal with McDonnell.

text.p: - Taiwan's Central Leasing Co said on Thursday it would team up with U.S. giant McDonnell Douglas to start a US$200 million global leasing firm to tackle aircraft shortages in the vast China market.
"We recently signed a letter of intent with McDonnell Douglas in Paris for the establishment of the joint venture," Central Leasing vice chairman J.C. Tung told Reuters.
Start-up capital of the proposed venture, Seanho Leasing Co, would be around US$200 million, of which Taiwan interests would contribute 80 percent, Tung said.
"We are seeking local investment partners in order to raise enough funds for the proposed project," he said.
Potential partners would include Formosa Plastics group, the Koo's Group, Shin Kong Life Insurance group and Cathay Life Insurance group, he said.
A formal agreement between Central Leasing and McDonnell Douglas would require further negotiation, Tung said.

Under the plan, the proposed venture initially would acquire some 150 to 200 McDonnell Douglas planes and lease them to fast-growing airlines, targetting mainland Chinese, southeast Asian and other carriers, Tung said.
The mass-circulation China Times estimated such a project would cost between T$400 billion and T$500 billion (US$14.3-17.9 billion) and yield annual sales of T$30-50 billion.
Tung dismissed those numbers, saying it was "still too early" to estimate finances and that a more detailed plan was needed. Central is Taiwan's number three leasing company.
Tung acknowledged that mainland China, Taiwan's longtime rival, was an attractive target market and an important reason behind his firm's decision to work with McDonnell Douglas.
"Given its huge size, the mainland market is definitely worth exploring," Tung said.
